classification.difficultyReason: Use four equal areas to count favourable regions.

content.prompt: A dart is thrown at the board shown opposite. There is an equal chance of hitting any point on the board. What is the probability of:

spec.description: Four equal square regions in a 2 by 2 board. Source lower-right yellow is represented by house orange; no event refers to its colour.
spec.mathematics: Each region has one-quarter of the total area; bottom row has one-half.
spec.answerVisibility: Only given coloured regions are visible.

answer.worked: One of the four equal squares is blue, so $P(\text{blue})=\frac14$.
Three of the four equal squares are not blue, so $P(\text{not blue})=\frac34$.

children.label: c
children.prompt: hitting one of the bottom two squares?

answer.worked: Two of the four equal squares are on the bottom, so $P(\text{bottom})=\frac24=\frac12$.
